dedupe_keys.name: selecting and scheduling an optimal subset of road network upgrades

description: Alex Stivala, Peter Stuckey and Mark Wallace publish code for selecting and scheduling road-network upgrades. Zenodo archives version 1.0.0 under MIT, and the public GitHub README identifies user-equilibrium traffic assignment and planning models. The research problem chooses upgrades under a budget to reduce vehicle-hours travelled, then schedules them over a planning period using the discounted value of time savings. This model can compare road investment sequences under alternative traffic assumptions. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this implementation. Coverage depends on the supplied network, demand and proposed upgrades; the repository does not provide a current national road inventory. A limitation is that repeated assignment solutions, objective weights and forecast demand can change the preferred schedule, and the cited preprint does not establish field benefits after construction. The archive was not downloaded or run, and computational speed or vehicle-hour results were not independently reproduced.
